message.content:
Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate marked tracheomegaly (dilated trachea) and extensive bilateral cystic bronchiectasis with multiple large cavities, which are hallmark radiographic features of Mounier-Kuhn Syndrome (tracheobronchomegaly). The progression to increased cavity size and number indicates worsening disease, requiring management focused on airway clearance (physiotherapy) and treating superimposed infections with antibiotics.
